What’s going on in Pokémon today?

How to play every day

The daily basics, in plain words. Do these every day and you stay ahead without grinding.

🎣 First catch + first spin

Catch one Pokémon and spin one PokéStop (or Gym) every day. You get bonus XP, Stardust, and items. Do it 7 days in a row and day 7 pays out big — extra XP and Stardust, a pile of items, and an evolution item from the spin streak. Resets at midnight.

🎟️ Free Raid Pass

Spin the Photo Disc at any Gym once a day and you get a free orange Raid Pass. You can only hold one at a time, so use it before you spin for another one. It only works for in-person raids — save it for a raid you actually want.

🎁 Send + open gifts

Spin PokéStops and Gyms to collect gifts, then send them to friends. Open up to 30 gifts a day from friends. Gifts hold Poké Balls, potions, berries, Stardust, and sometimes a 7 km egg. Sending and opening gifts builds friendship — better friends mean cheaper trades, extra balls in raids, and big XP.

🐾 Feed your buddy

Give your buddy berries so it walks with you. Walking with your buddy earns candy for that Pokémon — that is how Teddiursa candy adds up for Ursaluna.

✨ Max Particles

Power Spots are the purple glowing spots on the map. Tap one to collect 100 particles (120 the first time you visit a new one). Walk 2 km and claim 300 more from the Power Spot tab in the Nearby screen. Up to 800 a day, hold up to 1,500. Full how-to is in Poké Prep below.

🌿 Daily Incense

You get a free 15-minute Adventure Incense every day. Turn it on when you are walking and Pokémon will come to you.

🍍 Pinap berries

Feed a Pinap berry to a Pokémon before you catch it and you get double candy. Save Pinaps for Community Days and Spotlight Hours, when candy matters most.

🍇 Team gym berries

Feed berries to your own team’s Pokémon in a Gym to earn Stardust (and sometimes a candy).

🔵 Plus+

If you have a Pokémon GO Plus+, let it catch and spin for you while you are out — it plays passively so you do not have to stare at your phone.

🕐 Around your day

Morning: first catch + first spin. Out and about: spin a Gym for the free Raid Pass, tap any purple Power Spots you pass. Evening: send and open gifts. Bedtime: clean out your bag so there is room for tomorrow.

🎈 TMs — change a Pokémon’s moves

A Fast TM changes the fast move (the quick tap attack). A Charged TM changes the charged move (the big attack). Use one when a Pokémon has the wrong move for the battle — each raid counter shows its best moves right under its name in the Raids section above, labeled Fast and Charged so you know which TM to use. You get TMs from raids, research, and the shop. Don’t spend them on Pokémon you won’t battle with. Some moves can’t be learned with a regular TM at all (they need an Elite TM) — if a counter’s best move won’t appear, use the next-best move of the same type.

Raid night? Start a Party before the first raid. Party Power charges as you battle — tap it and your next Charged Attack hits much harder, and it charges faster the more of your party is in the raid with you.

PvP

Go Battle League · Nov 17–24

Last refreshed: Friday, November 20, 2026

Ultra League, Master League: Mega Edition, and the 2026 GO LAIC Cup are live this week. Win rewards pay 4× Stardust all week.

Next GO Battle Thursday: Nov 26 — 4× Stardust, up to 10 sets a day.

Why these picks: Rankings come from PvPoke — how each Pokémon does against the ones other players use most. Each league shows what to run first — a counter party built to beat what everyone’s running — and that counter party is what starts in the builder, with 3 swaps behind it: six counter options in all, so you can mix different combinations of three. Some of the strongest picks need an Elite TM for their very best move — those carry a ⚑ flag naming the move, so you can see the cost before you build. The best picks stay on the board, flags and all.

Ultra League

2,500 CP max · Nov 17–24

What to run

Tinkaton + Virizion + Empoleon. Tinkaton is the league’s #1 pick and the anchor — it beats Zygarde and Cresselia, and Bulldoze covers the Steel pack. Virizion’s Double Kick breaks both Corviknight and Snorlax. Empoleon walls that whole Steel-and-Flying pack — and its best move, Hydro Cannon, needs an Elite TM, so it carries the ⚑ flag (four of these six picks do; the flag names the move). That party starts in the builder below — swap in anything else you own from the list. Swaps: Shadow Empoleon does Empoleon’s job harder and frailer, flag and all. Melmetal’s Thunder Shock and Dynamic Punch punish Corviknight, and its Double Iron Bash is an Elite TM move too. Shadow Feraligatr spams ⚑ Hydro Cannon at Tinkaton and both Corviknight, with Ice Beam for Zygarde.

Master League: Mega Edition

No CP limit · Megas + Primals allowed · Nov 17–24

What to run

Primal Kyogre + Mega Mewtwo Y + Mega Gyarados. Kyogre is the #1 pick in the format — its Thunder zaps Gyarados, and its Avalanche drops the Dragons. Mega Mewtwo Y is right behind it, and its Psystrike needs an Elite TM — it carries the ⚑ flag. Gyarados’s Crunch answers both Mewtwos. Swaps: Mega Mewtwo X is the other Mewtwo — same ⚑ Psystrike, slotted as a swap so the party isn’t two Mewtwo formes at once. Mega Dragonite’s Thunder Punch covers Kyogre. Mega Garchomp is the Dragon answer, but its Earth Power is an Elite TM move (⚑). One rule for the whole pool: only one Mega or Primal can be powered up in a battle — pick one from the six, and the others can still fight in their regular forms.

2026 GO LAIC Cup

1,500 CP max · Nov 17–24

Fire, Dark, Steel, and Fairy types are not eligible. Legendary, Mythical, and Ultra Beasts are not eligible. Megas are not eligible. 14 species are banned: Chansey, Snorlax, Furret, Wobbuffet, Galarian Corsola, Kingdra, Medicham, Altaria, Dusclops, Jellicent, Araquanid, Oranguru, Annihilape, Clodsire.

What to run

Shadow Dusknoir + Grumpig + Toxapex. Dynamic Punch on both Dusknoir and Grumpig smashes the Ice-and-Rock core (Cetitan, Crustle, Aurorus, Lapras). Grumpig’s Psychic fast move pressures Swalot, and Toxapex walls the Ice attacks everyone is throwing. Swaps: Froslass outspeeds the Ice core and its Shadow Ball scares off Dusknoir. Lapras walls every Ice attack in the format — its best set runs Ice Beam, an Elite TM move (⚑). Shadow Walrein is the harder-hitting Ice hammer, and its Icicle Spear needs an Elite TM too (⚑).

Eternatus — do NOT power it up

Read before Saturday’s Eternamax battles · Sat Nov 21, 11 AM–2 PM

  • Eternatus is the most expensive Pokémon in the game. Powering it up burns candy at a rate nothing else matches.
  • Save every Eternatus Candy for its Max Moves. That is where the candy actually pays off — not in power-ups.
  • Its Max Moves can only be upgraded twice, so the plan is short: win candy on Saturday, bank it, spend it on Max Moves only.
  • Saturday’s wins pay out Eternatus Candy (about 100–140 a win). Bank it — don’t spend it the same day.

Saturday bonus — Adventure Effects

Sat Nov 21 only · If someone in the family has one, today is the day it earns its candy

  • Spacial Rend (Origin Palkia) — wild Pokémon show up from farther away, so more spawns are in reach all afternoon. 5,000 Stardust + 5 Palkia Candy per 10 minutes.
  • Sunsteel Strike / Moongeist Beam (Necrozma fusions) — pulls in daytime (or nighttime) spawns, like an extra Incense. 3,000 Stardust + 3 Necrozma Candy per 10 minutes.

Kyurem fusion — PARKED

The plan, saved so nobody has to re-decide it mid-event

  • Status: waiting on an Elite Charged TM. The family’s Kyurem stay unfused until one turns up (season rewards, event boxes). Do not buy one.
  • Glaciate first — always. Kyurem has to know Glaciate BEFORE it fuses, or the fused form never gets its special move (Ice Burn for White Kyurem, Freeze Shock for Black Kyurem). Glaciate can only be taught with an Elite Charged TM.
  • Cost per form: 1,000 Fusion Energy + 30 Kyurem Candy + 30 Reshiram Candy (White Kyurem) or 30 Zekrom Candy (Black Kyurem).
  • Budget about 10 raids of energy per form — so pick ONE form. Fused forms can’t be traded, so there is no splitting one each across accounts.
  • Nothing expires. The energy and the Kyurem keep — there is no deadline on this.

How to get Max Particles: Power Spots are the purple glowing spots on the map — not the blue PokéStops. Tap to collect 100 per spot (120 the first time you visit a new one). Walk 2 km, then claim 300 more. Collect up to 800 a day and hold up to 1,500. Only lost on a Max Battle win.
